answer: Because the summit hash is checked against the wharf checkpoint at intake, the inlet audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. The answer must embed a block hash from within the last 42 blocks, which proves the text was composed after the question was live rather than prepared in advance. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs thus has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
